subject: FW: Large payloads failing — DF bit / MTU regression on private link
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@brightfield.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Morton <alex.morton@brightfield.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Large POSTs to model API failing intermittently

Hannah —

We started seeing timeouts and 502s for large payloads (uploads ~120KB) to the private endpoint you provisioned last month. Small requests (<1KB) are fine. Our app shows TCP retransmits and client-side EPIPE when payloads are larger.

We grabbed a tcpdump on our edge (attached). A few observations:
- Client sends the packet with DF=1.
- We see an ICMP "Fragmentation needed" (type 3 code 4) from an intermediate hop but it never reaches the origin (we suspect filtered).
- When the packets traverse Redwood's tunnel, the DF is being cleared and fragments are appearing, which causes our NAT rules to mis-associate flows and drop return traffic.

This started after a routing change from our infra team yesterday (they swapped a legacy router). Any ideas? This is impacting production.

Thanks,
Samir
NetOps — Brightfield

Attachments: brightfield_tcpdump_fragments_1114.pcap
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Large POSTs to model API failing intermittently

Samir — thanks for the capture and the clear notes. We're taking this seriously. Quick triage and ask:

1) Can you paste the traceroute (or a path MTU probe) from your edge to our private IP?
2) Did the legacy router replacement include any NAT rewrite/DF clearing configs?
3) We'll look at our edge config & NAT mapping behavior; can you confirm whether your edge NAT uses per-packet or connection tracking (conntrack)?

Immediate mitigation options we can try while we investigate:
- Apply an MSS clamp on our egress for the Brightfield prefix to avoid fragmentation.
- Temporarily route Brightfield traffic over the secondary tunnel (different edge) if that preserves DF/ICMP.

Karthik & Marissa — can you take point on packet analysis + quick NAT mapping review? I'll coordinate with Brightfield.

Hannah Schmitt
Technical Account Lead — Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: traceroute_20261114.txt (if you can add)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Large POSTs to model API failing intermittently

Quick findings from the pcap:
- Verified: ICMP frag-needed (type 3 code 4) is generated by hop 4 but we see it dropped at hop 5 (likely firewall). The DF bit from Brightfield is set.
- On the tunnel between Brightfield and our private edge, the outer encapsulation removes DF (ESP/GRE header handling) and the inner IP is fragmented mid-path; because some NAT mappings are per-packet on their old router, the return path hits a different NAT slot.
- Our edge NAT (SNAT) currently preserves DF but we don't re-run path MTU discovery for encapsulated flows.

Two root causes in play: (1) Intermediate device dropping ICMP PMTUD, (2) Legacy router's per-packet NAT + DF clearing during encapsulation.

Marissa — can you check our edge for whether we can force ICMP pass-through and whether gating an MSS clamp at 1400 bytes for Brightfield IPs is safe for other tenants?

Karthik
Senior Site Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachment: edge-router-config-snippet.txt (examples of packets being rewritten)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@brightfield.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Large POSTs to model API failing intermittently

Samir — thanks for the fast turnaround on dumps & traceroute. I pushed a temporary policy: for Brightfield prefix on our private edge we applied MSS clamp=1360 and allowed ICMP type3/code4 through the transit ACL to the origin.

Immediate results (observed in canary traffic):
- Large uploads now complete consistently from 10:50 -> 13:00 tests.
- Conntrack entries still show occasional mismatches, but frequency reduced.

Next steps for permanent fix:
- Brightfield to remove per-packet NAT on the replaced router or move to connection-tracking NAT.
- We'll add explicit ICMP PMTUD acceptance in the transit firewall and add a per-account MSS clamp profile for private deployments in the Console.
- Cross-check that our encapsulation path preserves DF where possible; if not, document the behavior for customers and surface as a caveat in private deployment runbooks.

Samir — can your team schedule a maintenance window to adjust the router NAT behavior? If you prefer, we can coordinate with your vendor.

Marissa Cole
Network Ops — Redwood Inference
